headline: Safer updates: install keeps your team's changes, says what it would do first, and backs up the team folder

changes.title: install sets up the whole folder, and keeps your changes
changes.before: flightdeck install copied only flightdeck.html. The skills were a separate command, and skills --force replaced files your team had changed without keeping a copy.
changes.now: flightdeck install also adds or updates AGENTS.md and the skills for your AI assistant. Files still at an earlier default are updated; files your team changed are kept. When this version changed them too, the new default goes to .flightdeck/updates/1.15.0/ with a README.md to hand to your AI assistant. Add --app-only to install only the app.
changes.where: flightdeck install <team folder>

changes.title: See what an update would do first
changes.now: Add --check to install or skills to see what would change, without changing anything. It exits with 0 when there's nothing to do, 2 when updates are ready, and 3 when files need merging, so a script can tell.
changes.where: flightdeck install <team folder> --check

changes.title: Back up a team folder
changes.now: flightdeck backup copies the whole team folder to a dated folder in Flightdeck backups in your home folder, or wherever you name with --to. It never copies links and never puts a backup inside the folder it backs up.
changes.where: flightdeck backup <team folder>

changes.title: Install keeps a copy of every file it replaces
changes.now: Before install or skills replaces any file, even with --force, it saves the old one under .flightdeck/updates/<version>/replaced/ and checks the copy, so nothing your team had is lost.
changes.where: flightdeck install or skills

changes.title: AGENTS.md has a place for your team's own notes
changes.now: Flightdeck's instructions for AI assistants sit between two markers in AGENTS.md. Team notes, below them, are yours: updates never change them.
changes.where: AGENTS.md in the team folder

changes.title: A new team folder's starter checklist names you as owner
changes.before: Start a new team folder made the starter Check in code checklist with an example person as its owner.
changes.now: The starter checklist names whoever created the folder as its owner, and the folder records which Flightdeck set it up.
changes.where: Settings: Start a new team folder

headline: Five new step types: Jira sprints, deploys, health checks, GitHub pull requests and measurements

changes.title: Jira sprint steps
changes.now: A {jira.sprint} step starts or closes a sprint, moves its unfinished issues, or sets its goal, on a named board. Checking it can note the sprint link, plus the new sprint's name and dates when starting, or how many issues carried over when closing.
changes.where: The parts box and the Type list in the draft editor, under Tools.

changes.title: Deploy and health check steps
changes.now: A {deploy} step names the environment, what to deploy, its version, the deploy tool and what to roll back to; checking it can note the version that went out, a link and when it finished. A {verify.health} step names a dashboard, a metric, when it counts as healthy and how long to watch; checking it can note Pass or Fail, the value you saw and a screenshot or link.
changes.where: The parts box and the Type list in the draft editor, under Tools.

changes.title: GitHub pull request steps
changes.now: A {github.pr} step opens, reviews, approves or merges a pull request in a named repository. Checking it can note the pull request link, whether its checks pass, and the merge commit for a merge.
changes.where: The parts box and the Type list in the draft editor, under Tools.

changes.title: Measure steps
changes.now: A {measure} step records a number with its unit, like velocity or points carried over, so runs keep a history of it. When later steps need the number as a run detail, use a step with sets: instead, like the capacity step in the sprint start example.
changes.where: The parts box and the Type list in the draft editor, under General.

changes.title: The examples use the new types
changes.now: The sprint start example closes the last sprint, records velocity, carry-over and capacity, then starts the new sprint and sets its goal. The release example records the deploy and watches the error dashboard. A new example merges a GitHub pull request. Versions that use the new types still open and run in earlier copies of Flightdeck.
changes.where: The example folder.

headline: Fill in keeps the evidence you typed, and Done differently tells the truth about a refused save

changes.title: Fill in keeps evidence typed before it opened
changes.before: If you typed evidence on a step, then opened Fill in and saved it, Fill in started with empty evidence boxes and saving threw away what you had typed. Done then checked the step without it.
changes.now: Fill in starts with the evidence you already typed on the step, and saving it keeps that evidence with the step. Done records it.
changes.where: A run: the selected step, Record the result, Fill in.

changes.title: Done differently no longer says it saved when it didn't
changes.before: If the run was saved from another window or computer while Done differently was saving its correction, the step stayed unanswered in the team folder but Flightdeck said "Done differently… Saved on this computer."
changes.now: Flightdeck says the run changed elsewhere and shows "Correction saved; the step wasn't marked done." with Mark it now, which stays on the run until you act. If the save failed and is waiting for Try again, it says that instead.
changes.where: A run: Done differently.

headline: Runs get a workspace of their own, corrections replace Suggest a fix, and notes take files

changes.title: A run fills the window
changes.before: A run was a long page: a big header, details, roles and a recording banner pushed the steps below the fold, and the step panel scrolled with everything else.
changes.now: A run is a page of its own: a slim header with 7/14 answered, a strip saying who's recording with Pause, Hand off, Pick up or Take over beside it, then three panes that each scroll on their own: Phases, the checklist and the selected step. The strip also says what this window saved and when it checked the folder; a failed save or a conflict shows there with Try again or Compare copies.
changes.where: Runs: open any run.

changes.title: Next up, and one place to answer a step
changes.now: Next up, pinned atop the checklist, points at where the run stands (the next step, a blocked step, a gate to review), never at what you're looking at. The selected step shows how to do it, values to copy, evidence to record, Done, Blocked, N/A and notes. Done reads what you typed in its evidence boxes. Check the step Next up points at and the next one is selected, so Space keeps going.
changes.where: A run: the checklist and the selected step.

changes.title: Suggest a fix became Corrections
changes.before: Suggest a fix asked you to pick one of several kinds of problem, then describe it in your own words. The process page marked a suggestion fixed whenever any newer version was published.
changes.now: Correct this step starts on the wording, with a Before/After redline as you type; Change something else covers a missing step, the order, who does it, a screenshot or removing it. It never answers the step. Runs and receipts list their Corrections; on the process page the same one from several runs shows once, and anyone marks it applied or declines it with a reason.
changes.where: A run: Correct this step on the selected step (or press C). A process page: Corrections.

changes.title: Done differently
changes.now: Beside Done, the recorder can mark a step Done differently: say what happened, then choose Just this run or Fix the checklist too, which adds a correction. It follows every rule of Done, so required evidence still has to be there.
changes.where: A run: the selected step.

changes.title: What you type stays with its step
changes.now: Evidence typed into a step, an open Fill in and an unsent note stay with that step while you move around the run, and come back when you return; the row says Draft. Drafts belong to their team folder. Checking a step (row, Done, Space or Done differently) uses what was typed on that step only. While its Fill in is open or unsaved, Done waits and says "Save or cancel Fill in first."
changes.where: A run.

changes.title: Attachments with runs of dots in their names
changes.now: A file named like deploy..output.log is saved as deploy.output.log and stays listed with its note after a reload.
changes.where: A run: attachments on notes and corrections.

changes.title: Attach files to notes and corrections
changes.before: A note or a suggested fix could carry one PNG, JPEG or WebP screenshot.
changes.now: Drop files on the note box, paste them, or choose Attach: images (PNG, JPEG, WebP, GIF), PDF, text and logs (.txt, .log, .md, .csv, .json, .yaml) and .zip, up to 10 MB each and several per note. Images show as pictures; text opens as plain text; other files save a copy. A file that isn't allowed is refused next to the box with the reason.
changes.where: A run: the selected step's notes, or Correct this step.

changes.title: Keyboard, phones and screen share
changes.now: J and K open a folded phase they move into, X works like Space, and a held key checks one step. On a phone a step opens as a full-screen sheet with Close, Previous and Next. Screen share shows who's recording, a pause, and why a step is blocked; Back to the run returns to the same step and scroll.
changes.where: A run. Press ? for the keys.

changes.title: Plain words for your AI assistant
changes.before: Skill briefs and the Skills page used a technical term for the assistant that builds skills.
changes.now: Flightdeck now says "your AI assistant" everywhere: copy the brief for your AI assistant, and it builds or updates the skill.
changes.where: Skills, and a process page: Skills.

headline: Build a checklist from parts, with Undo, Redo and History in every editor and a clearer step-type editor

changes.title: The draft editor is a page of its own
changes.now: Editing a draft fills the window: a header with Done, save state, Builder or Markdown, Undo, Redo and History, Checks and Save, then side-by-side panes that each scroll on their own. The inspector has Selected, Checks and Preview tabs, and Preview marks the selected step. Parts fold to a rail of icons. A refresh comes back to the editor, and the browser asks before leaving unsaved edits.
changes.where: A process page: Edit.

changes.title: A parts box beside the builder
changes.now: Add phases, parallel lanes, gates and any type of step from a searchable parts box. Drag a part onto the checklist: only places it can go light up and the nearest says where it lands. Or choose a part, pick a place with the arrow keys, and press Enter. The new item is selected with its name ready to type over, and Undo takes it back.
changes.where: A process page: Edit, then the Builder. On a phone, Add part.

changes.title: Edit lanes, gates and phases in the builder
changes.now: Parallel lanes show side by side. Select a lane to rename it, change who works it, or delete it, keeping its steps or deleting them with it. A phase's form can delete the phase or remove its gate. A step's kind is one choice: Step, Must do or Automation planned. A part you just added takes its ID from the name you give it, until you save the draft.
changes.where: A process page: Edit, then select a lane or phase in the Builder.

changes.title: Undo, Redo and History in the checklist editor
changes.before: Only the builder had Undo. Typing in Markdown or saving the draft cleared it.
changes.now: Undo, Redo and History sit beside the Builder | Markdown switch, in both views, with one history for both. Undo names what it takes back, like Undo move, and says what it undid. Ctrl+Z or Cmd+Z undoes, Ctrl+Shift+Z, Cmd+Shift+Z or Ctrl+Y redoes, even while typing. Undo still works after a save; saving again is checked like any save.
changes.where: A process page: Edit. A selected step or phase also has History of this step or phase.

changes.title: Undo, Redo and History in the step-type form
changes.now: The step-type form has the same Undo, Redo and History and the same keys. Removing a field or evidence and undoing puts it back where it was, with everything it had. Each row has its own History.
changes.where: Step types: New step type, or Edit on a team type.

changes.title: A clearer step-type editor
changes.before: One long form: the ID first, hints between labels and boxes, every field crammed on one line, and a Save button that was disabled without saying why.
changes.now: A full page with Save, Undo and History at the top and a live preview of the type in a checklist and in a run. The ID comes from the label. Tags are chips, the icon is a grid, and each field is a card you open, reorder or remove. Save says what's missing and keeps you in the editor, and Done asks before you lose changes.
changes.where: Step types: New step type, or Edit on a team type.

changes.title: Undo never puts older text over newer work
changes.now: When the draft changes in the folder, or you take their version, restore a version or discard your changes, History marks the spot and Undo stops there. Changes before it stay listed but can't be undone, so Undo never brings older text back over someone else's work.

changes.title: Checklist, Flight plan or Markdown in one switch
changes.before: Markdown was a separate small button beside the Checklist | Flight plan switch, and it didn't show when it was on.
changes.now: The checklist panel has one switch: Checklist, Flight plan or Markdown. Markdown shows the version's source, read-only, with Copy. The choice stays while you move around.
changes.where: A process page, the checklist panel.

headline: Checklist versions this copy can't read are never run

changes.title: Versions this copy doesn't understand can't be started
changes.before: A checklist version written by a newer Flightdeck, or edited by hand or by an AI assistant with lines or step types this copy doesn't know, was listed like any other version. You could start or plan a run on it, and steps that shouldn't have applied showed as ordinary work.
changes.now: Such a version isn't offered to start, plan or pick. The process page and the version picker say why: update Flightdeck to run it. A plan made for it starts on the latest version you can run, and says so. A run started on it, or saved by a newer copy with details or a file format this copy doesn't know, opens read-only with the reason, and this copy never saves over it or plans another like it.
changes.where: A process page, the version picker, Start a run, and the run page.

headline: Planned runs, a flight plan view, a checklist builder, and organized step types

changes.title: Suggest a fix to the checklist
changes.now: Anyone in a run can suggest a fix to the checklist from a step, a phase or a screenshot: a missing step, wrong instructions, a bad screenshot (attach the right one), wrong order, wrong role, or something else. On the process page, anyone can accept or decline each one with a reason. Accepted ones show as fixed once a newer version is published. Copy fix brief hands them to your AI assistant.
changes.where: A run: Suggest a fix on a step or phase. A process page: Suggested fixes.

changes.title: See a process as a flight plan
changes.now: On a process page, switch the checklist to Flight plan to see its shape at a glance: phases from start to landing, gates as checkpoints, tracks side by side and linked processes. With runs of that version, it shows each phase's usual time and the step that most often goes off-script. It marks steps covered by skills built from that version. Choose a phase to go to it.
changes.where: A process page, the Checklist | Flight plan switch.

changes.title: Edit a checklist with the builder
changes.now: Edit a draft as an outline: phases as cards, steps as rows, gates as striped bars. Drag a step, or select it and press Alt+Up or Alt+Down, to move it. Change a step's text, type, roles, run details and fields in the side form, and add steps, phases and gates. It writes the same Markdown, changing only the lines you touched and never a step ID. Markdown is one click away.
changes.where: A process page: Edit, then the Builder | Markdown switch.

changes.title: Plan a run ahead of time
changes.now: Plan a run in the app: a name, the details you know, who does what and an optional time. Planned runs are listed by time under Runs and show on Home from a day before. Nothing starts until someone starts it.
changes.where: A process page: Plan a run.

changes.title: Plan another like this
changes.now: Duplicate any run into a new plan with its details and roles. Its answers, notes and gates are never copied, and details a step fills in during the run are left for the new run.
changes.where: A run, or its receipt: Plan another like this.

changes.title: Plans keep their version
changes.now: A plan starts on the version it was planned on. If a newer one is published first, the plan says so, shows what changed and switches with one click.
changes.where: Starting a planned run.

changes.title: Step types in groups, with tags
changes.now: Step types are listed in groups, like processes and skills, with a tag filter. Give a team type a group and tags in its form; built-ins are grouped as General, Tools and Automation. Reorganizing a type never marks a process or a skill as changed.
changes.where: Step types.

changes.title: Clearer while a step type saves
changes.now: While Keep mine saves, the conflict shows Saving… instead of buttons that would do nothing, and Cancel and Discard my changes leave keyboard focus somewhere useful.
changes.where: Step types, and the draft editor.

headline: Clear sections, and templates and step types you manage in the app

changes.title: Six clear sections
changes.before: Home showed everything at once: the run you were recording, setup, every run and the library.
changes.now: The top bar has Home, Runs, Processes, Skills, Step types and Settings, and always shows where you are. Home lists only what needs you, each with one button; nothing opens on its own.
changes.where: The top bar.

changes.title: One page for each process: read, edit and version its checklist
changes.now: A process is one page with its checklist in the middle. Read it, show its Markdown to copy, or choose Edit to change the draft in place, checked and previewed as you type; saving stops and shows both if the draft changed since you opened it. Pick an older version to look back or restore it. How runs go has typical times and who has held each role.
changes.where: Processes → a process.

changes.title: Start a new process
changes.now: New process asks for an ID, title, group, tags, run details, roles and owner, then starts a draft checklist in maps/drafts/ and opens it for editing.
changes.where: Processes → New process.

changes.title: See every step type, and create your own
changes.now: Step types lists every built-in and team type: what it's for and how many checklists use it, with its fields and evidence one click away. New step type builds one from rows of fields and evidence, checked as you go, with the checklist line and the file it will save. Edit a team type, or start one from a built-in. Your AI assistant does the same from a description with flightdeck-new-step-type.
changes.where: Step types.

changes.title: A clear Skills page, and a page for each skill
changes.before: Skills was a list mixed with processes, and clicking one opened its process.
changes.now: Skills shows the skills that need an update, the signed-off processes with no skill yet (each with Copy brief), and every skill by group and tag. Open a skill to see what changed under it and copy its update brief. The process page is shorter too: run times and who has held each role moved to How runs go.
changes.where: Skills, and Processes → a process.

changes.title: Light, dark, or match this computer
changes.now: A button in the top bar steps through Match this computer, Light and Dark, and Settings has the same choice. Each browser remembers its own.
changes.where: The top bar, and Settings → Appearance.

changes.title: Always know which run you're in
changes.now: On a run, a slim bar under the top bar keeps its name, process and version, where it is and how far it's got in view as you scroll, and the browser tab is named after the run, so several open runs are easy to tell apart.
changes.where: Any run.

changes.title: One place for the team folder and setup
changes.now: Settings has the team folder (open, change, start new, examples), the people list, Jira workflows, keyboard shortcuts, and the version.
changes.where: Settings.

changes.title: Checklists, not maps
changes.now: What a process's written-down steps are called is now a checklist everywhere: the process page, the editor, the docs and the skills for your AI assistant. Team folders and files are unchanged.
changes.where: Everywhere.

changes.title: The right words after copying a brief
changes.now: Copying a skill brief says to paste it to your AI assistant, and gate approvals in the checklist preview show as formatted text.

changes.title: Skills for any AI assistant, installed anywhere
changes.now: The bundled skills are plain SKILL.md files that any assistant that supports skills can use. They now go in .flightdeck/skills/ in the team folder, and flightdeck skills --to <folder> installs them anywhere else, such as your assistant's own skills folder or another repo. The old -map skill names are gone; use the -checklist ones.
changes.where: flightdeck skills, and Settings → Start a new team folder.

changes.title: A skill's source, wherever it lives
changes.now: A skill's page shows where its source is (a repo, a shared folder or a local path) as Source, and briefs ask for that path or link when you register a skill. The location field in skills/<name>.json is unchanged.
changes.where: Skills → a skill.

changes.title: A full guide on the package page
changes.now: The README now walks through the loop from map to skill, a sixty-second tour of the examples, every feature, the map syntax with an example that publishes as written, process-to-skill traceability end to end, the command line, the team folder, the skills for your AI assistant, how Flightdeck stays safe, upgrading from Preflight, and an FAQ.
changes.where: The package page on npm.

headline: Process-to-skill traceability, values that flow through a run, and a hierarchy for everything

changes.title: Preflight is now Flightdeck
changes.before: The app was called Preflight, in preflight.html, with AI assistant skills named preflight-*.
changes.now: It's Flightdeck: flightdeck.html, with AI assistant skills named flightdeck-*. Team folders, runs and versions carry over. A browser keeps examples and your name per file, so flightdeck.html starts those fresh; flightdeck install also updates an existing preflight.html, so people who open it keep everything.
changes.where: Everywhere.

changes.title: Install with npm
changes.now: npm install -g @troylar/flightdeck, then flightdeck open to try it, flightdeck install <team folder> to put the app there, and flightdeck skills <team folder> to add the skills for your AI assistant. No dependencies, nothing runs on install, no network.
changes.where: A terminal.

changes.title: See which skills implement each process
changes.now: Each process page lists the skills built from it: where each lives (any repo or folder), its own version, the process version it follows, and the steps it covers or the whole process. The map marks covered steps.
changes.where: Skills, on a process page; Home → Skills.

changes.title: Know when a process change affects a skill
changes.now: When a new version changes the steps a skill covers, the skill shows as needing an update, with the exact before and after; if its steps didn't change, it only needs its version noted. Copy the update brief for your AI assistant.
changes.where: Copy update brief, on a skill.

changes.title: Prove a version, then turn it into a skill
changes.now: Each version shows its run evidence: completed runs, clean ones, and what people did differently. With 3 clean runs the owner signs it off, and Flightdeck writes the brief an AI assistant needs to build the skill. The flightdeck-skill-brief skill does the same from the folder, with your AI assistant.
changes.where: Ready for a skill?, on a process page.

changes.title: Organize processes and skills in a hierarchy, with tags
changes.now: Maps and skills say group: (like Engineering / Releases) and tags:. Home shows processes and skills as foldable trees, filtered by tag.
changes.where: Home → Processes and Skills.

changes.title: Let a step set a run detail
changes.now: A step can say sets: tag. Checking it asks for the tag and saves it as a run detail, so every later ^tag (commands, messages, Jira fields) uses it. The start form leaves it out and says which step fills it in. Correcting it later sends the steps that used the old value back for a re-check.
changes.where: sets: in a map; the example release's merge step sets the release tag.

headline: Pause, parallel tracks, times, child runs, Jira fields and run history

changes.title: Pause and resume a run
changes.now: The recorder can pause a run and say what it's waiting for. While it's paused, steps and gates can't change and timers stop; Resume picks up where it left off, and paused time never counts in durations.
changes.where: Pause, in the recorder bar of a run.

changes.title: Work in parallel tracks
changes.now: A phase can split into tracks, each with its own role, shown side by side. Every track finishes before the phase's gate.
changes.where: ### Track: Name @role {#id} in a map.

changes.title: Scheduled times and a day timeline
changes.now: Steps and gates can have a clock time (at: or due:) or a due time after the run starts (after:). Each shows a badge, the Day timeline lists them in order, and the recorder's window says when one is coming up or late.
changes.where: Day timeline, under the run's headline.

changes.title: Run another process from a step
changes.now: A {run.process} step starts a linked run of another process, passing on the details it names. The parent step is checked when that run completes, or blocked if it stops, and the child links back to its parent.
changes.where: Start the run, on the step.

changes.title: Check transitions against your real Jira workflow
changes.now: jira/workflows.json in the team folder lists each issue type's statuses, transitions and the fields each transition requires. Maps can't publish a transition the workflow doesn't have, and a transition step asks for its required fields, with a hint for each and the value filled in from the run where the file says where it comes from.
changes.where: A Jira transition step; the process page shows the workflows.

changes.title: Add the team's own step types
changes.now: Each step-types/<id>.json in the team folder is a step type with its own fields and evidence, checked as strictly as a map and frozen into each publication.
changes.where: Team setup, on any process page.

changes.title: See how runs go and who has done each role
changes.now: Each process page shows outcomes, the typical time per phase, the steps that most often get blocked or done differently, and a grid of who has held each role and when.
changes.where: How runs go, on a process page.

changes.title: Phase headers stay in view
changes.now: While you scroll through a phase, its header stays pinned under the top bar with the phase's progress, so you always know where you are.
changes.where: Any run.

changes.title: Redraw only what changed
changes.before: Every change redrew the whole screen.
changes.now: Only the parts of the screen that changed are redrawn, so focus, the caret and anything you're typing stay exactly where they were.

changes.title: Examples that show everything
changes.now: The examples now come with a month of team history: earlier releases (one stopped early) behind the analytics and role grid, a release whose check-in ran as a linked child run with its Jira fields filled in, an incident in progress split into tracks, and a sprint start that's paused, with its meeting time coming up.
changes.where: Home → Try the examples (Reset examples to see them in a browser that already has the old ones).

changes.title: Fewer leftover save receipts and copies
changes.now: A save receipt that matches the current run is cleaned up instead of being shown as a conflict copy, and removing a copy also removes identical receipts.

headline: See what's new, and know when a newer copy is waiting

changes.title: Read what changed in each version
changes.now: What's new in the top bar shows the version you're on and the full release history: search it, filter by new, improved or fixed and by area, and see before and after for each change. A dot appears when there's a release you haven't seen, and a short notice appears once after an update.
changes.where: What's new, in the top bar.

changes.title: Know when a newer Flightdeck is in the team folder
changes.now: If someone saves a newer flightdeck.html at the top of the team folder, older copies say so in the top bar, so everyone can switch to it.
changes.where: The top bar, after opening or refreshing the team folder.

headline: Every save survives, on one computer or many

changes.title: Keep both versions when two windows save at once
changes.before: Two windows or computers saving the same run at the same moment could replace each other's change without a warning.
changes.now: Windows on one computer save a run one at a time. Across browsers and computers, each save first leaves its own receipt; a save that another one replaced shows up in the run as a conflict copy to compare and keep.
changes.where: The panel at the top of a run, when it has other versions.

changes.title: Give each window its own files
changes.now: Notes, history, plan decisions and screenshots are written by each window to its own files, so a duplicated tab or a second window can never overwrite them.

changes.title: Keep the newest change through slow refreshes and failed saves
changes.now: A refresh never brings back an older version of a run over a change you just made, a save still in progress, or one that failed. Try again always saves your newest change.

changes.title: Keep what you're still typing
changes.now: Finishing one note clears only that note. Text typed while it saved, other steps' drafts and their screenshots stay. Notes over 2,000 characters are refused with a message instead of being cut short.

headline: AI assistant skills for writing and improving maps

changes.title: Write, review and improve maps with your AI assistant
changes.now: Every team folder carries six skills for your AI assistant: write a new map, edit one, review one, learn from recent runs, plan a run and summarize the folder. A checker in the skills judges published versions and plan decisions exactly as Flightdeck does.
changes.where: Open the team folder with your AI assistant and ask for a skill by name, such as flightdeck-status.

changes.title: Start a new team folder with everything in it
changes.now: Start a new team folder adds you to people.json, a starter map, the guide for AI assistants and the Flightdeck skills. It refuses a folder that isn't empty.
changes.where: Home → Get started.

headline: Finish runs well, recover safely, and work faster

changes.title: Finish a run with follow-ups and map changes
changes.now: End run opens a short finish: add follow-ups with an owner and Jira ticket, review suggested map changes from "did it differently" answers and map-change notes, then choose the outcome. The receipt includes all of it, and follow-ups from the last 30 days show on Home.
changes.where: End run in any run you're recording.

changes.title: Compare and keep conflict copies in the app
changes.before: Conflict copies had to be compared by hand in the folder.
changes.now: A run with other versions shows a panel to compare each one, keep it (the current version is saved beside it first) or delete it. Nothing is merged without you choosing.
changes.where: The panel at the top of a run.

changes.title: Choose how to begin
changes.now: Home offers three paths: try the examples, open your team folder (with the OneDrive tip to keep it on this device), or start a new team folder.

changes.title: Run a checklist on your own
changes.now: Starting a run asks On my own or With others. Solo runs hide roles and screen sharing, and confirming a phase is one click.

changes.title: Refresh only what's open
changes.now: While a run is open, Flightdeck rereads just that run every few seconds. Published versions and finished runs are remembered, so large team folders stay quick.

changes.title: Easier with a keyboard and screen reader
changes.now: Single-key shortcuts can be turned off, dialogs return focus when closed, errors appear next to their field, form fields have stronger borders, and messages are announced.
changes.where: Press ? for keyboard help and the shortcut switch.

headline: Fill in values as they become known

changes.title: Fill in or correct a step's values mid-run
changes.now: Some values aren't known until the middle of a release. The recorder can fill in a step's details and evidence before or after checking it; each change is logged with its old value, and the map's own value stays visible.
changes.where: Fill in, on any step.

changes.title: Describe a step with only what's known
changes.before: A step type's usual fields were required before a map could publish.
changes.now: A step can name only what's known; a missing usual field is a tip, not an error. Evidence is required only where the map says require: or evidence:.

headline: Clearer headings and runs for one

changes.title: The same headings on every computer
changes.now: Headings use a built-in typeface, so Windows and Mac show the same thing, and code-style text is used only for commands, values and times.

changes.title: Runs for one person
changes.now: A run with nobody but you assigned drops the team wording, and a map can say runs: solo to skip assigning roles.

headline: Step types that fit the work

changes.title: Jenkins, pull request and Jira steps
changes.now: New step types for a Jenkins job, a Bitbucket pull request and a Jira issue, each with the fields that matter to it.

changes.title: Record evidence when you check a step
changes.now: Steps can record a build number, a pull request link, a decision or a review verdict. It shows on the step and on the receipt.

changes.title: Versioned process maps
changes.now: Write a process as a checklist map with phases and gates, publish it as a numbered version, and see every version with its change note and differences.

changes.title: Run a checklist together
changes.now: One person records while others follow along and add notes and screenshots. Gates approve exactly what they say, and changing a detail like the commit sends tied steps back for a re-check.

changes.title: Timers, deadlines and a receipt
changes.now: Start a step to time it, copy a deadline from the real tool to see a countdown, and copy a receipt into Jira when you're done.
